name: No Equipment (Bodyweight)
description: No external equipment required. The exerciser uses only their own body mass as resistance.

name: Standard Barbell
description: A straight Olympic barbell, typically 45 lbs (20 kg) for men's or 35 lbs (15 kg) for women's, used with weight plates. The standard for compound free-weight exercises including squats, deadlifts, bench press, and rows.

name: EZ-Curl Bar
description: A short, W-shaped barbell that allows the hands to grip at an angled position, reducing wrist and elbow stress during curling and tricep exercises.

name: Trap Bar (Hex Bar)
description: A hexagonal or diamond-shaped barbell that allows the lifter to stand inside the bar and grip handles at their sides. Used primarily for trap bar deadlifts, shrugs, and farmer's carries. Places less stress on the lower back than a standard barbell deadlift.

name: Safety Squat Bar
description: A specialty barbell with padded yokes that rest on the shoulders and handles angled forward. Allows the lifter to maintain a more upright torso during squatting movements and is easier on lifters with shoulder mobility limitations.

name: Smith Machine
description: A barbell fixed within steel rails that guides the bar in a vertical or near-vertical path. Provides stability and allows for safer solo training on pressing and squatting movements. The bar path is mechanically constrained.

name: Dumbbell (Fixed)
description: A short, handheld free weight with fixed weight, typically available in a set ranging from very light to very heavy. Allows independent movement of each arm, enabling a greater range of motion and unilateral training.

name: Adjustable Dumbbell
description: A dumbbell system that allows the weight to be changed by adding or removing plates or via a selector mechanism. Saves space compared to a full rack of fixed dumbbells.

name: Kettlebell
description: A cast-iron or steel ball with a handle. The offset center of mass creates unique loading demands compared to dumbbells. Used for swings, cleans, presses, Turkish get-ups, and carries.

name: Cable Machine (High Pulley)
description: A cable pulley system with the cable anchored at the top. Used for exercises such as lat pulldowns, face pulls, tricep pushdowns, and cable crossovers.

name: Cable Machine (Low Pulley)
description: A cable pulley system with the cable anchored at the bottom. Used for exercises such as cable rows, bicep curls, cable pull-throughs, and face pulls with the cable at face height.

name: Cable Machine (Dual Pulley / Functional Trainer)
description: A cable machine with two independently adjustable arms, each with a full range of pulley positions from floor to overhead. Highly versatile for unilateral exercises and movements at any cable angle.

name: Resistance Band (Loop / Mini Band)
description: A continuous loop elastic band used to add resistance to bodyweight exercises or assist with pull-ups and dips. Available in a range of resistances. Mini bands are smaller loops used around the ankles or knees.

name: Resistance Band (Tube with Handles)
description: A rubber or latex tube with handles at each end. Used as a portable substitute for cable or dumbbell exercises. Can be anchored to a door or fixed object.

name: Flat Bench
description: A padded bench with a horizontal surface used for pressing, rowing, and bodyweight exercises. The standard bench for flat bench press and chest-supported rows.

name: Adjustable Bench (Incline / Decline)
description: A padded bench with an adjustable back pad that can be set to flat, incline, or decline positions. Increases exercise variety for pressing, rowing, and curl movements.

name: Preacher Bench
description: A bench with an angled arm pad that supports the upper arm during curling exercises. Isolates the biceps by preventing shoulder involvement and momentum.

name: Pull-Up Bar (Doorframe)
description: A portable bar that mounts in a doorframe without permanent installation, used for pull-ups, chin-ups, and hanging core exercises.

name: Pull-Up Bar (Freestanding Tower)
description: A freestanding structure with a pull-up bar and often dip handles. Does not require attachment to a wall or doorframe.

name: Pull-Up Bar (Wall-Mounted)
description: A pull-up bar permanently mounted to a wall or ceiling. Sturdier than doorframe options and can support more load. Often used in home gyms.

name: Dip Bars / Dip Station
description: Parallel horizontal bars used for dips, L-sits, and other calisthenics movements. Can be a standalone station or part of a power rack or pull-up tower.

name: Weight Plates
description: Cast iron or bumper plates used to load barbells and other compatible equipment. Bumper plates can be dropped safely from height.

name: Power Rack (Squat Cage)
description: A four-post steel cage with adjustable safety bars and J-hooks for the barbell. The safest way to train squats and bench press without a spotter. Often includes a pull-up bar.

name: Squat Stand
description: Two independent uprights with J-hooks and adjustable safeties. More compact than a power rack but requires more careful positioning. Suitable for home gyms with space limitations.

name: Half Rack
description: A two-post rack open at the front, providing safeties and J-hooks with less steel than a full power cage. Saves floor space while still allowing safe barbell training.

name: Leg Press Machine
description: A sled-based machine where the user pushes a weighted platform away with their feet while seated or reclined. Primarily trains the quadriceps with significant glute and hamstring involvement depending on foot position.

name: Leg Extension Machine
description: A seated machine that isolates the quadriceps by having the user extend the knee against a padded resistance arm. The only machine that provides direct isolation of the quadriceps.

name: Lying Leg Curl Machine
description: A prone (face-down) machine that isolates the hamstrings by having the user flex the knee against a padded resistance arm.

name: Seated Leg Curl Machine
description: A seated machine that isolates the hamstrings. The seated position places the hip in flexion, which may provide greater stretch on the hamstrings than the lying version.

name: Lat Pulldown Machine
description: A cable-based machine with a horizontal bar or attachment pulled downward from above. Used for lat pulldowns and variations. Provides an assisted alternative to pull-ups.

name: Seated Cable Row Machine
description: A cable machine with a low-pulley and horizontal cable for seated rowing exercises. Allows a variety of handle attachments for different grip positions.

name: Chest Press Machine
description: A seated or reclined machine for horizontal pressing movements. Guides the arm path mechanically, requiring less stabilization than free-weight pressing. Available in plate-loaded and selectorized versions.

name: Pec Deck / Fly Machine
description: A seated machine for chest fly movements. The user pushes two padded arms or handles together in front of the chest. Isolates the pectoral muscles without loading the shoulder joint in the same way as free-weight flyes.

name: Shoulder Press Machine
description: A seated machine that guides the arms in a vertical pressing path, training the deltoids and triceps. Provides a guided movement pattern safer for those with shoulder instability.

name: Hack Squat Machine
description: A sled-based machine where the user stands on a platform angled backward and presses the sled upward in a guided track. Targets the quadriceps heavily while reducing lower back involvement.

name: Hip Abductor / Adductor Machine
description: A seated machine that trains hip abduction and adduction. The user sits and either pushes the pads apart (abduction) or squeezes them together (adduction). Used for targeting the outer and inner thigh muscles.

name: Standing Calf Raise Machine
description: A machine where the user stands with shoulder pads and raises their heels to plantarflex the ankle. Trains the gastrocnemius and soleus with the knees extended, emphasizing the gastrocnemius.

name: Seated Calf Raise Machine
description: A machine where the user sits with padded supports on the knees and raises the heels. The bent knee position reduces gastrocnemius involvement and places more emphasis on the soleus.

name: T-Bar Row
description: A barbell landmine-style row setup where one end of a barbell is anchored and the other is loaded with plates. The user rows the loaded end toward their chest. Targets the mid and upper back.

name: Hyperextension Bench (45°)
description: A bench angled at 45° with padded ankle supports, allowing the user to flex and extend at the hip while keeping the legs fixed. Used for back extensions, hip hinge training, and hamstring work.

name: Roman Chair (Hyperextension Bench 90°)
description: A hyperextension bench with a horizontal hip pad, allowing the torso to hang vertically. The 90° position provides a greater range of motion than the 45° bench for back extensions.

name: Gymnastic Rings
description: Two adjustable rings suspended from above, used for bodyweight pulling and pushing exercises. The unstable surface challenges stabilizing muscles significantly more than fixed bars.

name: Suspension Trainer (TRX-style)
description: A system of adjustable straps that anchor overhead, allowing the user to perform bodyweight pushing and pulling exercises with the feet or hands in the straps. Instability and leverage create scalable resistance.

name: Medicine Ball
description: A heavy, weighted ball used for plyometric training, core exercises, and partner drills. Can be thrown, caught, and slammed depending on the type.

name: Slam Ball
description: A heavy, non-bounce ball designed to be slammed forcefully against the floor or wall. Used for power and conditioning exercises. Unlike a medicine ball, it does not rebound.

name: Swiss Ball (Stability Ball / Exercise Ball)
description: A large inflatable ball used for core training, balance exercises, and as a bench substitute to introduce instability. Challenges stabilizing muscles during presses and core exercises.

name: Foam Roller
description: A cylindrical foam device used for self-myofascial release and flexibility work. Applied to tight muscles by rolling over them with body weight.

name: Ab Wheel (Ab Roller)
description: A small wheel with handles on each side, rolled forward from a kneeling position to train the core with an anti-extension challenge. One of the most effective tools for training the transverse abdominis and rectus abdominis under load.

name: Dip Belt
description: A belt worn around the waist from which additional weight plates or kettlebells can be hung. Used to add external load to bodyweight exercises such as pull-ups and dips.

name: Lifting Straps
description: Wrist straps that wrap around the bar to assist grip during heavy pulling exercises (deadlifts, rows, shrugs). Allows the lifter to train the target muscles beyond grip failure.
